top_categories.workout_context: 13,035ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
128ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At GFNY Villard de Lans, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Villard de Lans' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
At mile 60 of 101, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Road-specific control matters at GFNY Villard de Lans. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 101 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Villard de Lans. Train it until it feels boring.
13,035ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 101 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 13,035ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 13,035ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY Villard de Lans. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.weather: May in Villard-de-Lans, Isere, France. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before GFNY Villard de Lans. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY Villard de Lans’s 101 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: GFNY Villard de Lans includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at GFNY Villard de Lans rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 101 miles of mixed terrain in Villard-de-Lans, Isere, France.
